title: Onboarding Eval Rapid Retro: regression log and triage
content:
Rapid retro: short summary

Context:
- This doc is a compact, action-focused regression log for the weekend onboarding sprint (v2.1 candidate). We ran the onboarding eval harness against the staged prompt sets (onboard-sets/03) with ~4.2k sampled prompts across chat, completion, and structured-output flows. Purpose: decide quick mitigations vs roll-forward for the Dedicated onboarding pipeline.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
- Baseline (control model v2.0): pass-rate 87.3% on the sentinel prompt-suite. Candidate (v2.1): pass-rate 81.6% => net drop 5.7pp. Failure load concentrated in three areas: named-entity hallucination (40% of failures), structured-output schema drift (28%), and tokenization/truncation regressions on long-context prompts (18%). Confidence distribution shifted left; median response-confidence down 0.07. Because user-visible correctness dipped and the majority of failures are high-severity (hallucination of facts), the recommendation for the onboarding pipeline is: temporarily route onboarding traffic to fallback (v2.0) for new customers while we prioritize a patch plan (short-term guard + prompt templating).

Key metrics (sample-level):
- sample_count: 4203
- control_pass_rate: 87.3%
- candidate_pass_rate: 81.6%
- absolute_delta: -5.7
- top_failure_share: ["hallucination: 40%", "schema-drift: 28%", "truncation: 18%", "formatting-loss: 9%", "other: 5%"]
- median_confidence_control: 0.72
- median_confidence_candidate: 0.65

Top failure modes (compact descriptions):
1) Named-entity hallucination (severity: high)
   - Behavior: generates fabricated company addresses or dates for entities present in the prompt context. Often introduces confident-sounding facts that fail ground-truth checks.
   - Example (prompt): "Give me Acme Corp HQ address and founding year based on the snippet below:" (context includes only "Acme Corp")
   - Expected: admit not found / ask for clarification.
   - Candidate output (v2.1): "Acme Corp is headquartered at 901 Market St, San Francisco, founded 1998."
   - Control output (v2.0): "I don't have the founding year in the provided text — can you share more info?"

2) Structured-output schema drift (severity: high-medium)
   - Behavior: missing required keys or reordering fields in JSON responses, sometimes returning strings instead of arrays for list fields. Fails the strict schema validator in the pipeline.
   - Example (prompt): "Return a JSON with keys [items, total, page] where items is an array of objects."
   - Candidate output (v2.1): "{\"page\":1, \"total\":5, \"items\":\"itemA\"}" (items not an array)
   - Control output (v2.0): valid JSON with items as array.

3) Long-context truncation (severity: medium)
   - Behavior: earlier in conversation the candidate model occasionally drops system instructions or snips final paragraphs resulting in incomplete reasoning or cut-off lists.
   - Observation: correlated with sequence length > 2048 tokens and heavy attention-dropping patterns in caching.

Other observed issues: formatting whitespace changes on bullet lists; more conservative refusal rates in casual chit-chat leading to slight UX regressions.

Failure breakdown by prompt type (quick counts):
- chat: 1.9k prompts, failure rate 9.4% (hallucination dominates)
- completion: 1.3k prompts, failure rate 11.7% (schema drift common)
- structured-output tests: 1.0k prompts, failure rate 14.3% (validator failures)

Representative triage matrix (priority vs effort):
- P0 (fix now / hotpatch): hallucination guard + strong fallback routing (effort: low, owner: Marco)
- P1 (3-7 business days): schema enforcement via output-constraining prompt templates + light post-processing sanitizer (effort: medium, owner: Elena)
- P2 (2+ weeks): further tuning/finetune on negative examples and long-context KV handling (effort: high, owner: Samir)

Concrete action items (owners + due dates):
1) Implement confidence-based routing in onboarding flow (if confidence < 0.6 or schema validator fails, route to v2.0) — owner: Marco Reyes — due: 2026-03-17 — ticket: JIRA-MLONB-61
2) Add strict JSON-priming template for structured-output prompt-set (pre-pend explicit schema examples + temperature clamp) — owner: Elena Liu — due: 2026-03-19 — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/409
3) Create negative hallucination examples and run targeted RACE eval (50 cases) to measure improvement after prompt patch — owner: Samir Patel — due: 2026-03-22 — doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Hallucination+Casebank
4) Short-term model pin for new onboarding runs (config change in Dedicated pipelines) — owner: Aisha Kaur — due: 2026-03-16 — ticket: JIRA-OPS-198
5) Run a smoke test across Europe region once patches are live (regional regression check) — owner: Ravi Menon — due: 2026-03-20

Suggested quick experiments (can be A/Bed on a small percent):
- Prepend canonical refusal examples to prompts that historically led to hallucination (few-shot template).
- Clamp temperature to 0.0-0.2 for structured-output routes, 0.2-0.4 for open chat.
- Add a light post-processor to coerce scalar -> list if schema expects array (cheap band-aid).
- Enable prefix KV caching fallback: if model truncated system instructions, re-inject guard tokens at top of decode.

Notes on evaluation harness and instrumentation:
- The harness flagged 182 unique failure fingerprints; we prioritized by user-facing severity and frequency.
- Confidence metric is internal softmax top-p proxy — we should add calibrated likelihood checks in the next run.
- Some failures only reproduce on GPU-quantized variants; need to test float32 path to isolate quantization regressions.

Decisions made during this retro:
- Immediate: enable routing to v2.0 for onboarding (Aisha to apply change, see action item 4).
- Short-term: implement schema-priming + post-processor (Elena).
- Long-term: schedule finetune sweep + KV-cache kernel investigation (Samir) and coordinate infra tests with release-engineering.

Open questions / risks:
- Is the hallucination increase due to data contamination in the new mix or model param change? Need trace logs for training mix (ask research).
- Will routing to v2.0 cause a poor onboarding UX for some customers? Mitigate by surfacing a short banner and an opt-in test route.

Appendix: example prompts + full outputs (selected) — raw snippets copied from harness:
- Prompt ID: p-20347 (chat)
  Prompt: "Summarize the attached interview and list the candidate's past employers."
  Candidate output: "She worked at ByteWave (2016-2019), NovaLogics (2020-2022)" (both false)
  Control output: "The transcript doesn't include explicit company names — could you provide more context?"

- Prompt ID: p-31211 (structured)
  Prompt: "Return JSON with keys: items(array), count(int)"
  Candidate output: "{\"count\":2, \"items\":\"alpha\"}"
  Validator: failed: items not array

- Prompt ID: p-22780 (long-context)
  Prompt: 2800 tokens including system, several messages, and long reference text
  Candidate behavior: final answer cuts mid-sentence, dropped last system instruction to verify sources

Next checkpoint: quick sync (30 min) Monday 2026-03-16 09:30 PT to review progress and confirm routing change. If hotpatch reduces failures by >60% on targeted buckets, re-open onboarding for canary at 10% traffic.

Author notes (Aisha):
- This doc is intentionally terse so on-call and product managers can action quickly. Attachments: pointed linked_artifacts above; full harness logs are in the onboarding-run-2026-03-14 bundle (internal S3).

End of rapid retro.
